editorial:
Imagine moving to the quiet mountains of Tohoku to start over, only to have your past literally show up as a dead body. That is exactly what happens to Muroi, a man who just wants peace but keeps getting pulled back into the world of police work. You get to see him struggle with a promise he made to old coworkers while trying to be a father figure to the kids he has taken in. It is a slow-burn kind of story that feels more like a cozy drama than a loud action flick, focusing on family and secrets rather than just chasing bad guys.

The acting is top-notch and makes you really care about the kids growing up around Muroi. While the pacing is a bit slow at times, the mystery keeps you guessing until the end. If you enjoy stories about redemption and hidden truths, you will love this. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend.
endingExplained: The mystery wraps up when Muroi connects the body in the mountains back to the old Rainbow Bridge case. He discovers that the killer was someone hiding in plain sight, driven by old grudges. After a tense final confrontation, Muroi finally finds peace with his past. He chooses to stay with his foster children, proving that family is more important than his old career. It ends on a hopeful note about starting a new life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep crime mysteries and stories about found families.
